blocks.text: Agniveer — Indian Army, Indian Navy and Indian Air Force

blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Defence, Security & Emergency Services
ENTRY PATHWAY
Recruitment after school or equivalent
Academic eligibility varies by service, trade and recruitment notification.
CAREER AREA
Military service
Operational duties, technical trades, logistics, communications and service-specific training.

An Agniveer is a recruit enrolled under the Agnipath scheme for service in the Indian Army, Indian Navy or Indian Air Force. Agniveers undergo military training and serve in roles assigned according to the service, trade, aptitude, performance and organisational requirements.

This is different from a commissioned officer career. Agniveer recruitment is an enlisted personnel pathway, and the entry process, duties, training and future options differ across the three services.

blocks.label: Important career condition
blocks.text: Under the published Agnipath framework, service is generally for four years, including training. At the end of this period, up to 25% of a particular Agniveer cohort may be selected for regular cadre enrolment, subject to service requirements and performance. Retention is not guaranteed; candidates should plan for both continued military service, if selected, and civilian career options afterward.
A. Agniveer — Indian Army
Soldier / trade-specific role

Possible recruitment categories and trades vary by notification and may include General Duty, Technical, Clerk or Store Keeper Technical, and Tradesman categories. Candidates should check the current recruitment structure rather than assume every category is open in every cycle.

blocks.label: Useful preparation
blocks.text: General knowledge, mathematics, reasoning, science where required, physical fitness and the trade-specific syllabus.
B. Agniveer — Indian Navy
Sailor / assigned naval trade
Naval roles may involve technical systems, seamanship, operations, logistics or other assigned duties, depending on eligibility and service requirements.

blocks.label: Useful preparation
blocks.text: Mathematics, science, English, reasoning, general awareness, fitness and the relevant medical standards.
C. Agniveer — Indian Air Force
Airman / assigned IAF role

The Agniveervayu pathway offers service-specific training and assigned duties according to the current recruitment rules. The eligibility criteria for science and other subject groups must be checked in the applicable notification.

blocks.label: Useful preparation
blocks.text: English, reasoning, general awareness, mathematics and physics where required, physical fitness and medical eligibility.

Candidates must also meet the relevant age, nationality, marital-status where specified, physical and medical standards. Do not assume that the age range or eligibility from an earlier intake applies to a new one.

blocks.text: Prepare for the applicable running, physical-efficiency, measurement and other prescribed assessments.

The order of stages and the assessments used vary by service and intake. Always follow the official notification rather than relying solely on coaching material or social-media updates.
Year 1 — Military foundations

items.text: Complete initial military training.
Learn discipline, physical conditioning, teamwork and service procedures.
Develop basic knowledge of the assigned trade.
Learn equipment handling, safety and reporting.

blocks.text: Year 2 — Trade competence

items.text: Build proficiency in assigned duties.
Follow standard operating procedures and safety requirements.
Improve technical, operational or logistics skills according to the role.
Maintain fitness and professional conduct.

blocks.text: Year 3 — Performance and development

items.text: Strengthen operational competence and reliability.
Take on additional responsibilities when assigned.
Document eligible training and qualifications.
Begin researching civilian career pathways and further education.

blocks.text: Year 4 — Transition planning

items.text: Continue meeting service and performance requirements.
Follow the official process if considered for regular cadre enrolment.
Prepare for civilian employment, vocational training or higher education as a parallel plan.
Understand the discharge process, Seva Nidhi arrangements and applicable resettlement opportunities.

blocks.text: This is a planning framework, not a promise of specific duties, postings or promotions.

rows.text: Technical support and maintenance roles, where suitably qualified

blocks.text: The skills and qualifications gained depend on the actual trade, duties and training completed. Military experience alone does not automatically provide a civilian technical licence.

sections.heading: Pay, Seva Nidhi and service conditions

blocks.text: Under the original published Agnipath framework, the monthly package was set to increase over the four-year engagement, with a portion contributed to the Agniveer Corpus Fund and a matching government contribution. A one-time Seva Nidhi payment is provided on completion of the engagement, subject to the applicable scheme terms. The original published estimate was approximately ₹11.71 lakh, including interest assumptions.
Press Information Bureau
Important points to verify in the current terms:

items.text: Monthly pay and applicable allowances.
Corpus contributions and the final Seva Nidhi calculation.
Insurance and compensation provisions.
Leave, medical and other benefits during engagement.
Discharge conditions and the rules governing regular cadre selection.

blocks.text: Do not treat the original package figures as a guaranteed current take-home or final payout. Consult the latest terms issued by the relevant service. Under the published framework, Agniveers do not automatically receive the regular cadre's pension and gratuity benefits simply by completing the four-year engagement.
Press Information Bureau
A candidate should plan for more than one outcome.
Option A — Apply for regular cadre enrolment

Eligible Agniveers may be considered under the applicable service selection process. The published framework provides for up to 25% of each specific batch to be enrolled in the regular cadre, subject to organisational requirements and selection. This is not guaranteed.
Option B — Continue education or vocational training
Pursue an eligible degree, diploma, ITI course or other recognised qualification. Check the admission rules and available credit or qualification recognition before enrolling.
Option C — Enter civilian employment
Explore logistics, technical maintenance, operations, administration, security-related work where legally eligible, or other roles matching documented skills and qualifications.
Option D — Investigate public-sector opportunities

Check the current recruitment rules for CAPFs, state police, public-sector organisations and other employers. Any reservation, age relaxation or preference must be verified for the specific post and applicable policy.
A useful weekly routine balances the written examination, physical fitness and awareness of recruitment requirements.

blocks.label: Academic preparation
blocks.text: Study the subjects specified by the selected service and trade.

blocks.label: Reasoning and general awareness
blocks.text: Practise timed questions and revise regularly.

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: Build comprehension, grammar and communication skills.

blocks.label: Fitness
blocks.text: Follow a gradual, safe routine for endurance, strength and mobility.

blocks.label: Mock tests
blocks.text: Review mistakes and track progress rather than focusing only on scores.

blocks.label: Official updates
blocks.text: Check recruitment portals for application dates, corrigenda, eligibility changes and results.

blocks.label: Backup planning
blocks.text: Identify education and employment options for after the four-year engagement.
Avoid agents promising guaranteed selection. Use official recruitment channels and never pay unofficial fees.

Reset checklist
A well-prepared Agniveer candidate should demonstrate:

items.text: Eligibility for the selected service and trade.
Academic readiness for the relevant examination.
Physical fitness and medical eligibility.
Discipline, teamwork, adaptability and responsible conduct.
Willingness to complete military training and serve wherever assigned.
A realistic understanding of the four-year engagement and the selection-based nature of regular cadre enrolment.
A practical plan for continued service, further education or civilian employment.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Select the service and trade first, verify its latest official eligibility criteria, and build a preparation plan around the actual recruitment notification. Plan for the full four-year engagement rather than assuming automatic permanent service.
